title: Hazel and the Ember
premise: Lior Hartwell has survived the purge of the old gods by making herself small: a royal food-taster whose poison-trained body is her only armor, and whose knowledge of the Thornfell smuggler roads is her only leverage. But when prayers she never meant to speak begin to be answered, Lior learns the gods are not returning—they are being eaten, and the crown that feeds on them is erasing the country itself, village by village, from every map and memory. Guided by a dying hearth-god called Ember, who remembers her name when no one else can, Lior must lead a ragged company of the half-forgotten through roads that unravel behind them, seeking the Last Door out of a nation that is being unmade. In the end she discovers the Door opens only for someone willing to be remembered completely—every sin included—and she pays that price, carrying her country's true memory into exile so that one day it can be spoken back into being.
about_author: Xanthe Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing the personal effects of displaced families, an experience that haunts every page of their fiction. They write fantasy about people history tried to lose, and they insist the best maps are drawn by those escaping them.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet her mid-service at the royal court, detecting nightshade in a stew meant for the king, and learn how twelve years of controlled poisoning have made her body a ledger of survival. She keeps her head down, memorizes exits, and refuses the kitchen boy Tam's friendship. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence—the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: A Prayer Over Cold Porridge
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Sent to sample provisions in a mountain garrison, Lior mutters a childhood prayer over a cold meal—an old habit—and something answers. A warmth in the hearth speaks her full name, which appears in no surviving record. The god Ember claims he has been waiting inside her memory all along. Emotional beat: terror and a shameful flicker of longing.

chapters.title: What the Map Forgot
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with a brief interlude from Ember. Returning to the capital, Lior finds the village of Ashenmere gone—not destroyed, but erased; no one remembers it, including its own refugees standing confused at the gates. She realizes the crown's new Ministry of Continuity is feeding villages to something beneath the palace. Emotional beat: vertigo as reality proves editable.

chapters.title: The Company of Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Lior gathers the erased: a soldier who can't recall his own war, a midwife whose children have forgotten her face, Tam, who followed her and now barely recalls why. Each carries a fragment Ember can use as a compass toward the Last Door said to lie beyond Thornfell. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging among the discarded.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Using her old routes, Lior leads the company into Thornfell, but the mountains themselves are being rewritten—passes she knows dissolve into cliff face overnight. Ember burns brighter each time someone shares a true memory, teaching Lior that remembering is fuel, and forgetting is hunger. Emotional beat: grief for the country she thought she'd already left behind.

chapters.title: The Ministry's Hounds
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Crown inquisitors catch their trail, led by Chancellor Veyra, once a taster herself, who offers Lior immunity and restoration in exchange for Ember's heart-flame. Tam, torn between loyalty and his own fading memories, nearly betrays the group before choosing them. Emotional beat: temptation of safety versus the ache of being known.

chapters.title: Where the Gods Go to Be Eaten
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Beneath the palace lies the Maw, where the crown has been devouring gods for a century to power its continuity magic. Ember reveals the truth: Lior was born in Ashenmere, marked as a vessel, and her 'immunity' was preparation to host the final god. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve—her whole life was someone else's recipe.

chapters.title: The Door That Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the Door beyond Thornfell, the company learns it opens only for one wholly remembered self. Veyra attacks; the midwife and soldier fall holding the pass, buying hours. To open it, Lior must let Ember pour every erased memory back into her—including what she did to survive the purge. Emotional beat: climax of acceptance; invisibility finally surrendered.

chapters.title: Every Sin Included
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Flooded with total recall, Lior confronts her worst memory: as a child she traded her village's names to the first hunters to save herself. She speaks it aloud anyway, and the Door accepts her not despite the sin but because she owns it. She steps through alone, carrying the country's memory as Ember gutters out inside her. Emotional beat: devastating, cleansing sacrifice.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Ember
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Beyond the Door, in a borderland of other exiled nations, Lior plants a hazel sprig from Ashenmere and begins telling her country's story to anyone who will listen—each telling a seed. Tam arrives, having found his way by a memory she left him. Somewhere far off, a hearth warms without fire. Emotional beat: quiet hope; memory kept alive becomes belonging.
